notes: Web search: this session's allowance was already used up when this part began (the one search tried was refused: 200 of 200 used), so nothing here comes from a search. Everything was found by reading addresses directly with the kit's own polite reader (the honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt read first and obeyed, a second between requests to one host): the campaign websites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State (read on a scratch copy of the database with the files step: 11 of the 30 filed one), each government's own site, the two state parties' sites and the local party units they point to, the Legislative Reference Library, and Wikipedia articles opened by title. No search engine was read in place of the search tool, and the fetch tool was not used. About 200 pages were asked for in all. A second pass with web search restored would most help the eight candidates with nothing below, and the two judges, whose appointment dates are in news stories this part had no way to find.

Addresses that were tried rather than found on a page: with no search, likely web addresses were asked of the network (an address lookup is not a request to any site) and the few that exist were read. Two are recorded, each because the site itself names the candidate and the office: shanemekeland.com and maguireformayor.org. The same method found the Senate District 45 Republicans (sd45gop.org leads to www.sd45.org, which says it is prepared and paid for by the 45th Senate District RPM). About 1,800 names were asked about for the candidates who filed no website; the other few that exist were not recorded, because nothing ties them to anyone here: petersonforsheriff.com and sarahforschoolboard.org are the sites of other people in other states (a sheriff's race in a Hancock County, which Minnesota does not have, and a Seattle school board race); connieforschoolboard.com, retainjudgejohnson.com and votepeterson.org would not let a script in (robots.txt), so whose they are is not known; the rest are empty holding pages. Names repeat, and a common name in a web address proves nothing.

Not read, and left alone: Wilkin County, Swift County and the City of Mankato (each one's robots.txt tells every robot to stay out); the Minnesota Judicial Branch, onealforhouse66b.com and the Senate District 33 Republicans' site (each refused the kit's reader its robots.txt with 403, which the reader takes as "stay out"); tombergersonformn.com and the City of Eagan (each answered with a bot check, which was not worked around); the City of Minnetrista (403). The Governor's site was not asked, since part 10 found that it shows this machine a CAPTCHA. suezmyslony.com answered one request and refused five with 429 (too many requests), so only its home page was read. The Sixth Congressional District Republicans' listed address (mncd6gop.com) now leads to an unrelated gambling site and was not used.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, used as in part 10): the Senate District 49 DFL lists Kathy Nelson under "Local Candidates we support", not under its endorsements, so it is kept apart from endorsed_by; whether and how it is shown is John's decision. The Senate District 34, 50 and 55 DFL pages publish "Letter of Support" lists or rules; none names a candidate of this part.

The two sitting legislators (Liish Kozlowski, Shane Mekeland) have roster records, so only a website, endorsements and review items are recorded. Both review items are birth dates on which the Legislative Reference Library differs from the roster. No party page naming Mekeland's 2026 endorsement was found: the House District 27A Republicans' site is a single welcome page and the state party's nominees page lists statewide and congressional candidates only. His own site's words "Endorsed Republican Candidate" are not recorded: he is a sitting member, the party must publish an endorsement, and that page's text is partly from an earlier campaign.

The two judges (Lauren M. Johnson, Benjamin Charles Pieh): that each now holds the seat rests on a county's notice of offices to be voted for, which names every judicial seat's incumbent (the lead is part 16's): Stevens County's own notice for the Eighth District seat (official), and McLeod County's notice as its Auditor-Treasurer had it published in the McLeod County Chronicle for the First District seat (secondary). Neither says when the judge took the bench, and no page about either judge on a government's own site could be read, so neither has an official_page. With no web search, and newspapers' own search pages closed to scripts by their robots.txt (the West Central Tribune's was tried), no story of either appointment could be looked for.

Nothing found for eight candidates. Jamie Rezac and John Reigstad: their counties' sites ask scripts to stay out; Wikipedia's Wilkin County article (its table dated April 2023) names another person as the District 2 commissioner. Jason Peterson: Douglas County's Sheriff's Office page names the present sheriff only. Gregory Brinkman: he is not on the City of Mounds View's council directory, its Council Tenure List or its commission pages. Brian Ewoldt: not on the City of Savage's council or commission pages. Connie Lyscio, Sarah Marrow: not on their districts' present boards. Joyce Peterson: Glencoe-Silver Lake's own "Meet the GSL School Board Candidates" page (https://www.gsl.k12.mn.us/district/school-board/school-board-candidates) carries her answers as she submitted them, but they name no public office, campaign website or party, so there is nothing of a kind this file records.

Earlier runs under a party label: Wikipedia's articles on the 2022 and 2024 Minnesota House elections and the 2022 Minnesota Senate election were read for the four legislative challengers of this part (Knutson, Bruce, Bergerson, O'Neal); none of them appears, so no past_party is recorded for them. Paul Gardner's comes from the Legislative Reference Library.

Left out on purpose, though the pages read state them: family members, churches and parish membership, an illness, employers and job histories, schools and degrees, private and nonprofit board seats, service clubs, and personal endorsers. Offices that are private or association posts (League of Minnesota Cities, Municipal Legislative Commission, Metro Cities, Greater MSP, Regional Council of Mayors, a community foundation, a union presidency) are not listed as public offices, nor are a sitting commissioner's committee assignments.

verifier_notes: Every address in the file was opened again on 2026-10-02 with the kit's reader (honest User-Agent, robots.txt read first and obeyed). 69 findings checked: 63 kept, 6 removed, 4 reworded to match the page.

Reworded: Shannon Bruce's website (the Senate District 45 Republicans' candidates page links to its own page about her, not to her campaign site, so that clause was dropped); Mike Maguire's website (the page reads "Paid & prepared by"); Kathy Nelson's council entry (a sentence about the City's list of 2026 candidates had no address to check and was dropped); Laura Job's entry (the data call goes to app.membershipware.com, not to the City's own host).

Not re-checked: the statement that a website is the one "filed with the Secretary of State" rests on the researcher's reading of the Secretary's file; the verifier checked only that each site itself names the candidate and the office or place.

The Stevens County notice is a PDF and was read with ballot/pdftext.py: it lists "10 Benjamin Pieh" under "Eighth District Court (Five Seats)". The roster's birth dates quoted in the two review items (1988-01-12 and 1969-07-28) were confirmed in state_mn.sqlite, opened read-only; our record's "Ward W" for Brooklyn Park was confirmed in ballot_local_2026.sqlite.

For John to decide, unchanged from the researcher: Kathy Nelson's party_support ("Local Candidates we support", confirmed on the Senate District 49 DFL's page, and not an endorsement), and Andi Courneya's school district Policy Advisory Committee (confirmed on his site; an advisory committee, not an elected office).
